speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I rise today to discuss how we can build Parliament into a fairer arena for all.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: During the debate on the President’s Address, there was much discussion of how Opposition parliamentarians behaved and performed in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong openly called on the Opposition to offer a “serious alternative agenda” and noted that as Singapore develops into a mature democracy, it needs both a serious Government and a serious Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The question then is whether the current Parliamentary structures and processes support the work of a serious Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the last General Election, the Government has taken steps to recognise the Opposition in our Parliament with the appointment of Mr Pritam Singh, the hon Member for Aljunied Group Representation Constituency (GRC) and Leader of the Workers' Party as Leader of the Opposition and the provision of some resources to assist him to discharge his duties.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) supports these moves, we think that these steps are insufficient to recognise the Opposition’s role in our political system.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government can definitely do more to encourage a serious Opposition that is an integral part of a mature Parliamentary democracy.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Both the Government and the Opposition must play their part.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Ministers have discussed at length what the Government wants a serious Opposition to do.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us also discuss what a serious Government should do to strengthen our Parliamentary system.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since then, I have learnt a lot more about the processes and procedures of Parliament and participated in many lively and substantive debates.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Based on my personal experiences, some parliamentary processes may not be the most conducive to facilitate Members of Parliament (MPs), including those from the ruling party, to do their jobs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many MPs from both sides of the House do not come from a public policy or legal background and may require assistance to do such work.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, while there is a library in the Parliament and the librarians are very helpful, there is no other research support.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Obviously, the Government only wants MPs to be supported by volunteers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Furthermore, after 1997, only elected MPs are provided an allowance for the purpose of hiring a Legislative Assistant and Secretarial Assistant to support them.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Today, NCMPs have full voting rights equal to elected MPs and sit on Parliamentary committees.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I sit on the Public Petitions Committee and the Parliamentary workload has increased across the board, commensurate with the increasing complexity of our Civil Service and our Parliamentary system.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second observation: MPs could contribute more meaningfully to debates if the Government provides Ministerial Statements and other speeches to MPs and MPs provide Ministers with drafts of their speeches beforehand.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would be a win-win situation for all as it enables MPs and Ministers to debate on the substantive issues and further the discussion, instead of having to divine whether the questions have been answered by the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The ultimate objective of the debates in this Parliament are to arrive at the best policy for Singaporeans, not to win a Parliamentary debate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In that spirit, I have provided this Adjournment Motion speech to the Speaker and the Leader of the House prior to today’s delivery.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope this has enabled the Government to prepare a more substantive response to the issues and suggestions that I have raised in this speech.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The third observation: MPs could benefit from more flexibility around time-keeping, especially when it comes to Question Time or the Committee of Supply (COS) debates.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Time-keeping may be important to keep our processes efficient but I think more Parliamentary time should be provided to ensure that every Member who wants to ask a question can do so.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is especially true during the COS, where many Members have been unable to ask supplementary questions because of the guillotine time and billions of dollars of expenditure are just approved like that.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Having more substantive debates on policy would go a long way to enable Singaporeans to become better-informed on public policy and make the Government more accountable.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Flowing from my observations above, I have several suggestions for improvement, which fall into three major groups.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first group is aimed at better supporting MPs in carrying out their legislative duties.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, the Parliament Secretariat should be given resources to set up a research department.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Two, the allowance to hire Legislative Assistants and Secretarial Assistants should be increased and extended to NCMPs and NMPs.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is timely for the Government to review the Legislative Assistant scheme for NCMPs and NMPs, as it had promised to do so in 1997.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government should not use the risk of such data being misinterpreted or being used for other purposes as justification for not releasing it.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second group of suggestions is aimed at providing MPs with more time to question the Government and to discharge their duties as legislators.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One, we should introduce an “Opposition hour” during the first day of every Parliamentary Sitting to discuss subjects chosen by the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are likely to cover current topics which have the most public interest.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is not new and is done in other Westminster parliaments, such as the UK and Canada.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, in the UK, the Leader of the Opposition has 17 days where he can select the topics for debate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These debates cover a wide range of issues, from government policy to current events.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This also provides a platform for the Opposition to hold the Government to account, challenge its policies and decisions and propose alternative policies or solutions to issues facing the country.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would allow for debates to conclude substantively.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Speaker, obviously, would still have the discretion to end the debate if he is of the view that further questions being asked by MPs are not covering new substantive ground.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The third group of recommendations is aimed at strengthening the role of the Opposition in our Parliamentary system.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PAC's role is to scrutinise the Government's financial performance and use of public funds.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As such, it is important that the PAC is seen as independent and impartial.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many Westminster parliaments ensure this by having an Opposition MP chairing the PAC.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This was also the case in Singapore until 1968 when there were no more Opposition MPs in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first PAC Chairman under a People's Action Party (PAP) Government in 1959 was AP Rajah, who was an Independent.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second was Mr Lim Huan Boon, who was from the Barisan Sosialis.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As it has been over 40 years since Opposition MPs returned to this House, I believe it is timely to again embrace our Parliamentary convention of having an Opposition Member chairing the PAC.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PPC plays an important role in providing a platform for citizens to voice their concerns and grievances to the Government.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that the PPC is seen as objective and non-partisan, and having an Opposition Member as a chairperson can help to ensure this.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the UK, there is no rule that the Petitions Committee must be chaired by an Opposition Member, but this is currently the case.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What we are asking for is a fair arena for all and access to data and resources.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Opposition lacks access to the resources of our excellent Civil Service.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Handicapped by this lack of resources, alternative policies created by the Opposition will not have the same breadth and depth of the Government's.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The PSP echoes the views of the Leader of the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have made many suggestions that will enable us to better discharge our duties as Opposition MPs and NCMPs to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I urge the Government to seriously consider these suggestions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government must pay more attention to discussing serious alternative policies with us and spend less time deflecting and avoiding uncomfortable questions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On our part, we will continue to do our best to discharge our duties as a rational and responsible Opposition party in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This House comprises both the Government and the Opposition.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is to be a first-class Parliament that works amicably and constructively for the good of Singapore, it must be a fair arena for all.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I also thank him for providing his speech in advance, a departure from his norm in respect of his more recent Adjournment Motions and Motions, but quite understandable, given his proposal, and well appreciated.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, to provide additional resources for MPs, NCMPs and NMPs; second, to provide Ministerial speeches in advance and opportunities for Opposition to raise matters; third, more flexibility in time keeping; and fourth, chairmanship of certain Select Committees.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, on the issue of resources for Members, this is something that we review from time to time.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On this, there are two separate points, namely, the difference between the allowances for elected MPs and NCMPs and NMPs; and the quantum of the allowances for hiring Legislative and Secretarial Assistants.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As such, in principle, it is reasonable to differentiate between the support the elected MPs and NCMPs receive.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On the second, in terms of the allowances given to elected MPs, whether it be the general allowance or the allowances for hiring a Legislative Assistant and a Secretarial Assistant, we do not differentiate between PAP MPs and Opposition MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The amount given to elected PAP MPs and the elected Opposition MPs is exactly the same, which is fair.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The PAP backbenchers make do with exactly the same allowances as the elected WP MPs, save for the Leader of the Opposition (LO).

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I also wish to highlight that the LO gets more resources than the PAP backbenchers and the PAP Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) chairpersons.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is an example of how we review and adjust according to the circumstances.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong has called for a research department to support all MPs, costing $1 million for a start.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: His justification is that, and I quote, "many MPs, from both sides of the House, do not come from a public policy or legal background and may require assistance to do such work".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While many PAP MPs do not come from such backgrounds either, they are not asking for this.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They have been able to work within the allowances currently allocated to them.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They also often pool their Legislative Assistant allowances to hire full-time Legislative and/or Secretarial Assistants to support two or more MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They do not confine themselves to the Legislative Assistant allowance, but often also draw upon their MPs' allowance to top up the sum.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is quite open to Opposition MPs and NCMPs to do the same.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: What is of note, however, is that the absence of such research facilities has not, in any way, deterred the PSP from asserting its ability to advance policy positions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In PSP's 2020 manifesto, they said that the Government's response to the economy was, I quote, "a patchwork of policy tweaks without addressing the fundamental factors affecting Singaporeans" and what was needed was "a paradigm shift" and to "look for workable alternative solutions going forward".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They said, and I quote again, "Progress Singapore Party's manifesto offers a better alternative to the current problems that we are facing as a nation" and their manifesto refers to various economic, social and political policies.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, though, Mr Leong espouses the view that "The Opposition lacks access to the resources of our excellent Civil Service.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Handicapped by this lack of resources, alternative policies created by the Opposition will not have the same breadth and depth of the Government's." That was his statement earlier.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is a marked contrast between the statements in PSP's manifesto and Mr Leong's statements in Parliament today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Civil Service works with the elected government of the day.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ultimately, it is the Ministers who decide on the Government's agenda and set the major direction of policies being implemented.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These policies are not presented by the Civil Service fully formed, with all the Ministers having to do is simply read out the policy speech in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ministers provide political guidance to the Civil Service to deliver results and the Ministers have to take responsibility for the same.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If Mr Leong needs more information, he can obtain those through PQs and during COS cuts; and he has done so.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the end of the day, the key to better debate in Parliament lies in understanding the main issues at hand, acknowledging our fundamental realities and constraints and taking not just the easy decisions but also the hard ones.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is not through making unending requests for ever more detailed data, which are then used as an alibi for not offering more constructive ideas or better alternative policies during debates.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In reality, we actually provide more data than most countries.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will lean forward to provide what is reasonable and practicable, but we cannot fulfil every whim.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Minister Tan See Leng explained this at an earlier Sitting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Next, Mr Leong requests that Ministers provide their speeches to MPs in advance.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In exchange, he proposed MPs provide "drafts" only of their speeches beforehand.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The reality is that the system is designed such that MPs can always engage and debate the Ministers, irrespective of when the Minister's speech is delivered.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: First, those with strong public interest, where multiple PQs have been filed and those addressing important matters which have to be dealt with expeditiously and at short notice or are not suitable to be dealt with under other mechanisms.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MPs can seek clarifications from the Minister on the Ministerial Statement.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Policy speeches delivered outside of Parliament, which are publicly reported, Members would have enough time to go through these and raise issues in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In most of these situations, MPs have more than ample opportunity to engage the Ministers on their speeches through a wide array of mechanisms: PQs, supplementary questions, Motions, Bills, Adjournment Motions, clarifications and COS cuts.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In fact, if anything, the advantage is with the MPs, because most of these mechanisms are not time-bound.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: MPs may deploy these days, weeks, months and sometimes even years after the Minister's speech was delivered, as Mr Leong himself has done, for example, on manpower issues.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Of course, there may be instances where notice is not possible, for example, when the Minister is responding in the course of an ongoing debate or market-sensitive matters, such as tax announcements.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But what is possible is to ensure that there is enough time for MPs to digest what has been said, respond and then have an informed substantive debate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is because every Sitting is an opportunity for MPs, whether PAP or Opposition, to raise topics of their choice and to hold the Government to account, challenge policies and decisions and propose alternative policies through these mechanisms.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They can do this through PQs, moving full Motions for debates, as NMPs are doing at this Sitting, or moving Adjournment Motions, as Mr Leong is doing today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Leong's next proposal is, in effect, that there should be unlimited time for PQs and COS cuts.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While I can understand why, from his point of view he would like that, this would not be a good idea.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It would be the surest way of triggering Parkinson's Law – the adage that work will expand to fill the time allotted for its completion.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have already seen that happen with PQs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The time for PQs has increased considerably, given more Sittings.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, instead of allowing us to deal with more PQs, it has resulted in more, and often repetitive, supplementary questions on the same topic.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where flexibility is required, Mr Speaker has exercised his discretion to allow it, examples being the extension of time to enable supplementary questions on HDB's Ethnic Integration Policy and on Keppel Offshore & Marine.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parliament time is finite and questions and debates cannot go on without end.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Setting time limits ensures that questions stay focused, answers stay on point and more can be accomplished.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Let us reflect for a moment and ask if we really think that would be the case.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The better solution is the one that we already have in place under the rules.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The PAC and the PPC are Standing Select Committees.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A select committee is a committee of Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Standing Orders (SOs) provide that the composition of each standing select committee should reflect the balance between the Government benches and the Opposition benches in Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And if you think about it for a moment, that is fair – because it reflects the proportion of Government and Opposition MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SOs provide that the Speaker chairs the PPC, which is, again, fair because he chairs the whole Parliament – a position to which he was elected by Parliament at the beginning of the term.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And the Parliament which elected him was, in turn, elected by the people, who also decided the proportion of PAP MPs and Opposition MPs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Speaker appoints the Chair of the PAC, an authority conferred on him by Parliament through the Standing Orders, and that is also fair because it gives flexibility to choose an appropriate Chair having regard to the technical content involved.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Hence, the chairmanship of the select committees is drawn from the authority of the people and we should respect that.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In any case, Opposition Members serve on the select committees and are entitled to ask questions and argue issues fully.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is no reason to think that they have not done their job properly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The real issue is how to do this effectively.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The answer lies not in changing the rules, but rather, for MPs to develop the skills of listening, using the existing rules more effectively, to make a contribution to the debate and show that they are deserving of the trust that voters have placed in them.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Order, the time allowed for the proceedings has expired.
